It's fun gameplay loop but it is too frustrating for me, currently. The premise of the game is that you have an ever increasing amount of coal to supply to keep playing. The first day it's 40, and on Day 15 it's 40,000. If you fail to provide the amount you lose and restart entirely from scratch (there's no general passives over multiple runs). What makes it fun? There's RNG in how each day's map is generated with the ore veins and powerups you can get for that run. Some maybe crazy powerful weapons, some may be passive bonuses for the player, and others may be bonuses for workers you can employ. In addition, there's a strategic element of purchasing upgrades to help you mine faster, hold more items, fly, upgrade workers, etc. all at a cost of gold. You get gold based on what ores you mine, with coal = 1 gold and a diamond 4,000 gold for example. If you fill your quota early, you can prioritize mining higher value resources to bring back. But there's a risk as anything not brought back in time doesn't count in the final tally! In the first map, progression works by going down into heavier concentrations of ores. These are harder to mine and require more damaging utensils. But the difference between the dirt layer on top and the red/orange layer further down is ~5 coal per block versus ~500. So the goal is to get deeper and deeper and access more and more resources. What makes it frustrating? After the several rounds, I hit my skill / strategy cap and I can't unlock any more of the game. I get to Day 15 and lose, again and again. I've tried different utensils (differing pickaxes, unlocks, guns); different employee configurations (trying to optimize miners with collectors), but I always lose on Day 15. To unlock the next profession after the shaman you need to beat day 15 with the starting role. So I'm stuck. There is not any feedback that I have found for how to do better. It also sucks having really powerful utensils and abilities and then spending 10 minutes getting halfway as strong as you just were again - only to repeat this (for someone like me) ad infinitum with no way to progress. My suggestion to the dev(s) is to: 1. Implement a skill tree for the player to spend experience on to allow them to tailor their experience in a certain way. Want to use pickaxes and do classic mining? Here's a way to start with ladders and a better pick. Purchases on these items are discounted. Want to organize your company? Here's a skill that replaces a pick with a command function to order your miners and collectors around. In this way you still have the RNG, but the premise of each dig is still under the control of the player. Instead of going through 8 days to really start specializing, this would allow the player to begin with a specialty to try from the beginning and then pivot or respec their skills if they don't enjoy it. 2. I'd recommend another pass at the buy menu for items and their costs. Not to make the game "easy" but where a doofus like myself can get to day 16 after 12 hours, because at this rate I'll never play again. The outcome will be the same. 3. Ladder interactions and a magnet item / ability. Ores get stuck in corners or pass through blocks and I spend almost a minute or more each round trying to jump off the ladder to the collection box at the top. I wish there was an easier dismount similar to Terraria. When you are on the ladder you should be on it. Any movement up or down is the player. Getting off should require a jump. If you move left or right then instead of jumping you move as normal. Up or no move is a jump as usual.

What would happen if the flash game Motherload had a ticking clock and light idle-game mechanics. If you are on this page I feel like I don't need to explain to you what Motherload is, but if you want some context then there is nothing stopping you from playing it. I personally really liked Motherload when I was young, and Coal LLC has taken some obvious inspiration and seemed and indeed has more to offer. I've grown a bit of a distaste for idle or incremental games over the years, whenever something needs to bust out scientific notation I sigh, and when my gear that cleared everything in a second in one area is effectively worth nothing in the next I just want to quit, but that isn't the big problem here. No the problem is difficulty. You just scale too quickly. I have played to the true ending four times, once on a character that an achievement told me was extremely hard, and to my recollection the closest I came to not making the quota was just having 125% of it, and that was on my first day on my first playthrough. On the extremely hard character I mentioned, the final challenge was to deliver something along the line of 1 000 000 coal by my lonesome. I managed to bring in something like 1E+10. There is basically no randomness either, so you figure out a strategy that works real quick. I had fun, but I didn't ever feel like I needed to figure out some deep strategy or pull off some impressive movement. I just pick up my acid gun, walk to the mine, load sixteen tons, grow a day older, and somehow go deeper into coal-based debt. I'd recommend it if you have a tolerance or like for incremental sorts of games, or have some nostalgia for Motherload. I do, and I think that I at least got my money's worth.
